2_time.predicted: installed about 15.6 ms a step; deferred between 9.3 and 15.0 ms a step, the lower end if launching 212 ranges a token costs nothing once no wait stands between them, the upper end if the waits were never the cost and the launches are
2_time.result: installed 13.972 ms a step and deferred 13.432 (the 27 answers with seconds on both sides, 13,320 steps: 186.11 s and 178.91 s). An answer's deferred seconds over its installed seconds: median 0.9732, least 0.8439, most 1.044; 20 of the 27 were faster deferred. The three calls took 76.12, 70.61 and 62.85 s installed (209.58 s) and 71.93, 68.75 and 61.37 s deferred (202.05 s), each with its model load.
2_time.held: the deferred side is inside the predicted range, near its upper end: taking the 212 waits once is worth 0.54 ms of a step's 13.97, about 4%. The installed side was faster than predicted (13.97 against 15.6): the machine's load average was 4.58 at this run's launch and 8.83 at its exit, and 5.94 and 12.32 at the launch and exit of recorders-beside-original, the run the 15.6 came from (the launching shell's own lines, repeated under provenance).

failures_only: The gain is 4%, not the 40% the lower end of the range allowed: the waits at the kept outputs are not what a kept token pays for. What it pays for is launching 212 separate ranges of nodes a token where the plain decode launches one graph: about 4 ms of a step by subtraction (13.43 less the plain decode's 7.9 and the recorder's records' 1.4 to 1.6), which this run does not measure directly.

The installed side's time was predicted from one earlier run at a higher load and came out 10% lower: a recorder's milliseconds a step move with the machine's load, and only the two sides of one run, alternated, compare.
what_this_changes: A copy of each wanted output taken on the card's own queue, with one wait a split, is the same computation as the installed stop at each output: 30 of 30 answers' files are the same bytes. Reading the outputs back without stopping is established as byte-exact on this card, engine and model; it is the base any further change of how the outputs are kept stands on.

By itself it is not worth adopting: 4% of the generation (about 8 s of a capture) for a second engine library and a new reader protocol. No capture, reading or protocol is changed; controlled-bf16-7 and the installed engine stay.

What is left of a kept token above the plain decode is the scheduler's 212 launches of small ranges. Removing it means computing a split as one graph, as the plain decode does, with the wanted outputs kept from reuse and read after it: a change of how the scheduler allocates the graph (the wanted outputs must survive to the end), which this patch does not make. Whether the engine computes the same bytes when a split is one graph and not 212 ranges is not known and is the next question; it is a separate declaration.
Nothing here bears on the hypothesis; no model was changed and no answer's content was compared or judged.
